newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on auction forecast.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on auction forecast.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 45 basis points at 17.10 percent on Monday due to what traders said were forecast falls in primary rates.
"Demand and liquidity were heavy. The market was still optimistic when it opened due over domestic inflation data and U.S. rates standing still," a fixed-income analyst said.
"The figures modified the outlook for inflation and that underpins a downward trend in (primary) rates," he added.
Banco de Mexico announced last week that domestic consumer prices rose by a lower-then-expected 0.48 percent during the first half of May.
The Federal Open Market Committee, meanwhile, decided not to change U.S. base rates.

Traders said bellwether 28-day Cetes rates could fall by up to 75 basis points at Tuesday's central bank auction. The 28-day primary Cete was assigned at 18.07 percent last week. Banco de Mexico drained 3.403 billion pesos from the market through three direct Cetes sales and seven repos.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended down 20 basis points at 18.60 percent.
Liquidity of 153 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank participation.
